1: There is fearlessness, purity of being and steadfastness in the yoga of knowledge. There is giving, self-restraint and sacrifice, study of the scriptures, austerity and straightness.
2: There is non-harming, truth, freedom from anger, giving up, peace and not slandering. There is compassion towards beings, freedom from greed, gentleness, modesty and freedom from fickleness.
3: And there is vigour, forbearance, firmness, cleanliness, freedom from malice and the absence of excessive pride. These belong to one born to the divine endowment, descendant of Bharata.
4: Hypocrisy, arrogance and conceit, anger and harshness too, and ignorance: these belong to one born to the demonic endowment, son of Pṛthā.
5: The divine endowment is held to lead to release, the demonic to bondage. Do not grieve, son of Pāṇḍu. You are born to the divine endowment.
6: There are two creations of beings in this world, the divine and the demonic. The divine has been described at length. Now hear from me about the demonic, son of Pṛthā.
7: Demonic people understand neither engaging in action nor ceasing from it. There is no cleanliness in them, nor even right conduct, nor truth.
8: They say that the world is without truth, without foundation and without a lord, that it is born of one with another and has desire as its cause. What else?
9: Holding to this view, these people whose self is lost, small in buddhi, fierce in their deeds and hostile, come forth to destroy the world.
10: They resort to desire that is hard to fill, and they are full of hypocrisy, pride and intoxication. Out of delusion they seize on false notions, and they act with impure vows.
11: And they are given over to immeasurable anxiety that ends at death. They hold the enjoyment of desires to be the highest thing, convinced that this is all there is.
12: Bound by hundreds of ropes of hope and devoted to desire and anger, they strive by unjust means for hoards of wealth, so that they can enjoy their desires.
13: They think: I have gained this today, and I shall get this wish too. This much is here, and this wealth will be mine as well in its turn.
14: I have killed that enemy, and I shall kill others too. I am the lord, I am the enjoyer. I am successful, strong and happy.
15: I am wealthy and of high birth. Who else is there equal to me? I shall sacrifice, I shall give, I shall rejoice. So they think, deluded by ignorance.
16: Led astray by many thoughts, covered by a net of delusion and attached to the enjoyments of desire, they fall into an impure hell.
17: Thinking highly of themselves, stubborn, full of the pride and intoxication of wealth, they offer sacrifices that are sacrifices in name only, with hypocrisy and not according to rule.
18: They resort to egoism, force, arrogance, desire and anger. Envious, they hate me in their own bodies and in the bodies of others.
19: Those haters, cruel and inauspicious, the lowest of men, I hurl ceaselessly through the cycles of birth into demonic wombs alone.
20: Having fallen into a demonic womb in birth after birth, the deluded never reach me at all, son of Kuntī. From there they go to the lowest state.
21: This is the threefold gate of hell, which destroys the self: desire, anger and likewise greed. So one should give up these three.
22: A person freed from these three gates of darkness, son of Kuntī, practises what is best for the self. From that, such a person goes to the highest state.
23: One who casts aside the rule of scripture and acts at the urging of desire does not attain success, nor happiness, nor the highest state.
24: Therefore scripture is your measure in settling what is to be done and what is not to be done. Once you know the action that the ordinance of scripture declares, you ought to do it here.
